elaras_silver_ring.name: plain silver ring
elaras_silver_ring.lore: A small ring of tarnished silver, polished smooth by a child's restless fingers. It holds no enchantment and no hidden power, only the fierce love of a little girl who believed it was the most precious thing in the world. Perhaps, in a way, she was right.

ring_magic_res_a.name: ring of magic resist
ring_magic_res_a.lore: Some monk scratched three letters around this pewter band, V R S, the way a scribe shortens a prayer he knows by heart: Vade retro Satana, 'Get back, Satan.' The abbreviation has outlived the monk. Hexes aimed at the wearer arrive weakened, as if they had to push through a closed door first.

ring_drain_res_a.name: ring of drain resist
ring_drain_res_a.lore: In the 1190s the English canon William of Newburgh wrote down, with some embarrassment, several reports of dead men who left their graves at night and wasted the living. Villagers in such places wore red jasper against them. This ring is of that kind: the grave-chill that saps a body does not get past it.

ring_levitate.name: ring of levitation
ring_levitate.lore: The old Acts of Peter tell how Simon the Magician rose into the air over Rome to prove his power, and how the Apostle Peter prayed him down again. Whoever hollowed this silver band learned the first half of the trick and wisely stopped there. Its wearer walks a hand's breadth above pits and floodwater.

ring_invisible.name: ring of invisibility
ring_invisible.lore: The Cyclopes made three gifts for the war against the Titans: the thunderbolt for Zeus, the trident for Poseidon, and for Hades a cap that hid its wearer from every eye. Perseus borrowed that cap to escape Medusa's sisters. A sliver of the same craft sits in this clear stone.

ring_hasted.name: ring of haste
ring_hasted.lore: Herodotus admired the Persian king's couriers, who rode in relays from Sardis to Susa and were stopped, he wrote, by neither snow nor rain nor heat nor darkness. A courier's ring like this one was handed from rider to rider with the message. Everything around its wearer seems to move through honey.

ring_clairvoy.name: ring of clairvoyance
ring_clairvoy.lore: Odin has a high seat in Asgard called Hlidskjalf. When he sits in it he sees into all the worlds and everything that anyone is doing there. This band of onyx gives a mortal one small corner of that view: the rooms and corridors nearby, laid out in the mind like a drawn plan.

ring_displace.name: ring of displacement
ring_displace.lore: The poet Stesichorus insisted that Helen never went to Troy at all. The gods sent a phantom in her shape, and the Greeks and Trojans fought ten years over an image while the real woman waited in Egypt. This obsidian ring plays the same trick on a smaller scale: blows land where its wearer only seems to stand.

ring_curse_teleport.name: ring of teleportitis
ring_curse_teleport.lore: Hera sent a gadfly to torment Io, and its sting drove her across the known world without rest. The strait she swam is still called the Bosporus, the Ox-Ford, after her. The cracked stone in this ring holds a sting of the same sort. Its wearer is forever being sent somewhere else.

ring_curse_aggravate.name: ring of aggravation
ring_curse_aggravate.lore: The hunter Actaeon saw Artemis bathing, and the goddess turned him into a stag. His own fifty hounds caught the scent and ran him down, never knowing their master. Something in this gaudy ring carries that scent. Every beast in earshot wakes hungry and turns toward the wearer.

ring_curse_fumble.name: ring of fumbling
ring_curse_fumble.lore: A thieves' guild in some forgotten port punished a member who stole from his fellows by locking a lead ring on his hand. He never again held a lockpick, a purse or a knife for longer than a breath. The guild is gone. The ring went on looking for hands.

ring_curse_slow.name: ring of slowing
ring_curse_slow.lore: Zeno of Elea argued that swift Achilles could never overtake a tortoise with a head start: each time he reached the place it had been, it had crawled a little farther. The philosophers called it a paradox. Whoever wears this black iron band lives inside it, always a step behind.

amulet_regen_jade.name: amulet of regeneration
amulet_regen_jade.lore: The Han princes of China believed jade kept a body whole. Prince Liu Sheng went to his tomb in a suit of more than two thousand jade plates sewn together with gold wire. This pendant is carved from the same stone on the same hope, and it works better on the living: cuts close, bruises fade.

amulet_hasted.name: amulet of speed
amulet_hasted.lore: Heralds paint the martlet, a swift or swallow, without any feet, because people long believed the bird lived its whole life on the wing and never came to rest. A fowler's wife strung these hollow bones for a son who was always late. He was never late again, nor ever quite still.

amulet_invis.name: amulet of invisibility
amulet_invis.lore: Country people said the fern bears an invisible seed on Saint John's Eve, and that whoever catches it on a white cloth at midnight walks unseen. Most who tried caught only dew. Someone caught the real thing once and stoppered it in this glass phial.

amulet_levitate.name: amulet of levitation
amulet_levitate.lore: The Egyptians called iron 'metal of heaven,' because the first iron they knew fell from the sky; a dagger of it lay in Tutankhamun's wrappings. This locket holds a pitted lump of the same sky-iron. It has never quite accepted the ground, and it lifts its wearer a little clear of it.

amulet_clairvoyant.name: amulet of clairvoyance
amulet_clairvoyant.lore: In 1252 Clare of Assisi lay too ill to leave her bed for the Christmas Mass. She said afterward that she saw and heard the whole service on the wall of her room, as plainly as if she knelt in the church. The sisters of her order carved this eye of dark stone in memory of it.

amulet_displace.name: amulet of displacement
amulet_displace.lore: Marsh folk call it the fool's fire: a pale light that hangs over the bog at night, always a few steps from where it appears, leading travellers off the causeway. A fen-dweller trapped one in smoky quartz. Now the wearer is the light, and every spear thrown at it finds only reeds.

amulet_fire_res.name: amulet of fire resistance
amulet_fire_res.lore: Pliny wrote that the salamander is so cold it puts out fire by touching it, and merchants on the Silk Road sold cloth that would not burn as 'salamander's wool.' This pendant hangs on a cord of that cloth. It has been through a furnace and came out cleaner.

amulet_cold_res.name: amulet of cold resistance
amulet_cold_res.lore: The Norse say the end will be announced by Fimbulwinter: three winters running with no summer between them, snow driving from every quarter. A northern mother painted this locket white and filled it with ash from her hearth, so that her children would carry the fire with them when it came.

amulet_shock_res.name: amulet of shock resistance
amulet_shock_res.lore: Sailors in a thunderstorm sometimes see blue flame dancing on the mastheads and burning nothing. They call it Saint Elmo's fire, after Erasmus, their patron, and take it as a sign he is watching. A ship's cooper twisted this charm from copper wire so the saint's fire would know where to go.

amulet_poison_res.name: amulet of poison resistance
amulet_poison_res.lore: Andromachus, physician to the emperor Nero, improved the old royal antidote by adding the flesh of vipers, on the reasoning that the snake must carry its own cure. Apothecaries sold his theriac for fifteen hundred years. This fang set in silver follows the same logic, and it seems to hold.

amulet_sleep_res.name: amulet of sleep resistance
amulet_sleep_res.lore: In the garden of Gethsemane the disciples fell asleep three times while their Master prayed, and he asked Peter whether they could not watch with him one hour. Monks who rise for the night office remember it. This small bell-shaped medal was a vigil-keeper's, and no drowsing spell gets past it.

amulet_magic_res.name: amulet of magic resistance
amulet_magic_res.lore: When Odysseus went to face the witch Circe, Hermes met him on the path and pulled a herb from the ground: black at the root, with a flower white as milk. The gods call it moly. Circe's wand did nothing to him. A dried root of the kind hangs on this cord.

amulet_drain_res.name: amulet of drain resistance
amulet_drain_res.lore: At the edge of the world Odysseus dug a pit and filled it with blood, and the hungry dead came crowding up to drink. He sat with his sword drawn across the trench and held them back. Silver braided the old way does the same work at the throat, and asks less of the arm.

amulet_curse_teleport.name: amulet of teleportitis
amulet_curse_teleport.lore: The prophet Habakkuk was carrying a bowl of stew to the reapers when an angel caught him by the hair and set him down in Babylon, over the lions' den, to feed Daniel. Then the angel carried him home. This split pendant keeps the journey and has lost the angel and the purpose.

amulet_curse_slow.name: amulet of slowing
amulet_curse_slow.lore: The Gospel says it would be better for a man to have a millstone hung about his neck and be cast into the sea than to lead a child astray. A magistrate with a taste for scripture had these grey medals made for his prisoners. They weigh almost nothing in the hand and a great deal on the neck.

dragonslayer_ring.name: Dragonslayer's Ring
dragonslayer_ring.lore: When the dragon woke, old King Beowulf ordered a shield made entirely of iron, because he knew linden wood would burn. Eleven picked men went with him to the barrow. Ten ran for the trees. Wiglaf alone stood in the fire beside his lord. This scorched gold ring came out of that hoard, and it remembers which of them stayed.

shadow_walker_ring.name: Shadow Walker's Ring
shadow_walker_ring.lore: A matte-black ring that seems to absorb light from its surroundings, worn by the leader of an ancient thieves' guild who specialized in assassinations too dangerous for ordinary operatives. Its gold and venom-glands were stripped from the same dead king; the band still smells faintly of nightshade. The wearer's blood stops noticing poison.

philosophers_ring.name: Philosopher's Ring
philosophers_ring.lore: Inscribed with a miniature version of the Philosopher's Shard's ouroboros, this ring was worn by the original dungeon philosopher on the hand that held their quill. The metal warms to the touch when unknown things are nearby; ancient inquiry traveled through the fingers.

ring_protection_silver.name: ring of protection +1
ring_protection_silver.lore: Since before the Crusades, soldiers have carried the ninety-first Psalm into battle, written small: 'He shall give his angels charge over thee.' A silversmith engraved the verse inside this ring in letters too fine to read without a glass. Blows aimed at the wearer land a little wide.

ring_protection_gold.name: ring of protection +2
ring_protection_gold.lore: Before the battle at the Milvian Bridge in 312, Constantine had his soldiers mark their shields with the Chi-Rho, the first two letters of Christ's name in Greek. He won Rome that day. Officers of the later empire wore the sign on gold bands like this one, and trusted it more than their mail.

ring_protection_adamantine.name: ring of protection +3
ring_protection_adamantine.lore: The Greeks named the hardest thing they could imagine adamas, 'the unconquerable.' The sickle of Kronos was made of it, and Virgil gave the gate of Tartarus columns of solid adamant that neither men nor gods could break. A filing from such a pillar was worked into this dark, heavy ring.

ring_speed_quicksilver.name: ring of speed
ring_speed_quicksilver.lore: The alchemists named quicksilver for Mercury, the swift messenger, because it is the one metal that runs. No smith can make a ring of it. This grey band is the nearest anyone has come, and it hums on the finger like a struck bell. Its wearer is always a moment ahead.

ring_sustenance_amber.name: ring of sustenance
ring_sustenance_amber.lore: During the great drought the prophet Elijah lodged with a widow of Zarephath who had one handful of meal and a little oil left. She fed him first. The jar of meal and the cruse of oil did not run out until the rains came. A drop of that oil, they say, hardened into this amber.

ring_strength_dragonbone.name: ring of giant strength
ring_strength_dragonbone.lore: Og, king of Bashan, was the last of the giants. The Book of Deuteronomy records that his bed was made of iron, nine cubits long and four wide, and that it was kept on show in Rabbah for anyone who doubted. This ring was carved from a knucklebone that would fit such a bed.

ring_constitution_diamond.name: ring of endurance
ring_constitution_diamond.lore: Pliny believed a true diamond set on an anvil would shatter the hammer and the anvil before it broke itself. He was wrong about the stone and right about the idea. The clear gem in this ring lends its wearer that stubbornness: the body keeps going long after it has every reason to stop.

ring_intellect_prismatic_deep.name: ring of brilliance
ring_intellect_prismatic_deep.lore: The Ptolemies searched every ship that docked at Alexandria and took its books to the Library. The scribes made copies, and it was the copies that went back to the owners. A librarian there cut this stone so that it throws one beam of light into many, as a reminder of what the collection was for.

amulet_life_saving.name: amulet of life saving
amulet_life_saving.lore: Alcestis agreed to die in her husband's place, and did. Heracles, a guest in the mourning house, went out to the tomb, waited for Death to come for his due, and wrestled him until he let her go. This warm gold medal remembers the hold. It works once.

amulet_spell_turning.name: amulet of spell turning
amulet_spell_turning.lore: King Balak of Moab hired the seer Balaam to curse Israel and took him up three mountains to do it. Three times Balaam opened his mouth and a blessing came out, and the curse fell back on the man who paid for it. The spiral cut in this medallion turns ill words the same way.

amulet_truesight.name: amulet of true sight
amulet_truesight.lore: On the plain before Troy, Athena told Diomedes she had lifted the mist from his eyes so that he could tell god from man in the fighting. He wounded two immortals before nightfall. A lens of this clear stone does the same for lesser eyes: the hidden thing is simply there.

amulet_reflection.name: amulet of reflection
amulet_reflection.lore: Perseus never looked at Medusa. He watched her in the polished bronze of the shield Athena lent him and struck backward at the reflection. The face of this medallion is polished the same way, and a hex that meets it tends to go home to its maker.

amulet_titan_constitution.name: amulet of titan constitution
amulet_titan_constitution.lore: Zeus chained Prometheus to a crag in the Caucasus for stealing fire. Each day an eagle came and tore out his liver, and each night it grew back whole, so that the punishment could go on. The blood-red stone in this pendant came from that rock. It makes a body very hard to finish.

amulet_archmage_intellect.name: amulet of archmage intellect
amulet_archmage_intellect.lore: Odin wanted one drink from Mimir's well, where wisdom is kept, and Mimir's price was an eye. Odin paid it. Later he hung nine nights on the windswept tree, wounded with a spear, to learn the runes. The violet stone here is said to be cut from the well's rim. It did not come cheap either.

ring_curse_drain.name: ring of life drain
ring_curse_drain.lore: Erysichthon cut down an oak sacred to Demeter, and the goddess sent Hunger to breathe on him as he slept. He ate his herds, sold everything he owned for food, and in Ovid's telling ended by gnawing his own limbs. This cold ring has the same appetite, and the wearer is nearest.

amulet_curse_drain.name: amulet of doom
amulet_curse_drain.unidentified_name: a sword-shaped pendant on a hair-thin chain
amulet_curse_drain.lore: Damocles told the tyrant Dionysius of Syracuse how fortunate a king must be. Dionysius sat him on the throne at a banquet with a sword hung over his head by one horsehair. Damocles lost his appetite. Whoever wears this pendant sits in that chair, and the hair is fraying.

ring_of_gyges.name: Ring of Gyges
ring_of_gyges.unidentified_name: a plain band that seems to blur at the edges
ring_of_gyges.lore: In Plato's Republic, Glaucon tells of Gyges, a Lydian shepherd. An earthquake opened the ground, and inside a hollow bronze horse he found a dead man wearing a gold ring. Turning the bezel inward made him invisible. He won over the queen, killed the king and took the throne. Glaucon's question: with such a ring, would anyone stay just?

ring_of_the_nibelung.name: Ring of the Nibelung
ring_of_the_nibelung.unidentified_name: a heavy gold ring with a tiny rune
ring_of_the_nibelung.lore: Loki took this ring from the dwarf Andvari to pay the blood-price for Otr, and Andvari swore it would be the death of everyone who owned it. Fafnir killed his father Hreidmar for it. Sigurd killed Fafnir and was murdered in his own bed. Gunnar and Hogni sank the hoard in the Rhine and died in Atli's hall without saying where.

andvaranaut.name: Andvaranaut
andvaranaut.unidentified_name: a golden ring that seems lighter than it should
andvaranaut.lore: Andvari the dwarf lived as a pike under a waterfall, guarding his gold. Loki borrowed the sea-goddess Ran's net, hauled him out, and took everything. The dwarf begged to keep one small ring, because with it he could make his wealth grow again. Loki took that too. Its name means Andvari's Gift, which was the dwarf's idea of a joke.

draupnir.name: Draupnir
draupnir.unidentified_name: a golden ring of incredible craftsmanship
draupnir.lore: Forged by the dwarven brothers Brokkr and Sindri alongside Mjölnir, Draupnir drips eight new gold rings of equal weight every ninth night. Odin placed it on Baldr's funeral pyre, and Baldr sent it back from Hel as proof of his existence. Gold finds its way to the hand that wears it.

ring_of_eluned.name: Ring of Eluned
ring_of_eluned.unidentified_name: a green ring of twisted ivy-metal
ring_of_eluned.lore: In the Welsh tale of the Lady of the Fountain, Owain chased a wounded knight through a castle gate. The portcullis dropped behind him, cut his horse in two, and left him trapped between the gates. The maiden Luned passed him a ring through the bars: with the stone turned inward and a hand closed over it, she said, no one would see him. No one did.

brisingamen.name: Brisingamen
brisingamen.unidentified_name: a necklace of four interlocked golden torcs
brisingamen.lore: Four dwarves made Freyja's necklace: Alfrigg, Dvalin, Berling and Grer. Loki crept into her bower as a fly to steal it, and Heimdall fought him for it on a skerry, both of them in the shape of seals. Thor once wore it under a bridal veil to win back his hammer. When Freyja weeps for her lost husband Od, her tears are red gold.

talisman_of_troy.name: Palladium of Troy
talisman_of_troy.unidentified_name: a small wooden figure of armed Athena
talisman_of_troy.lore: The Palladium was a wooden image of armed Athena that fell from the sky into Troy, and the city could not be taken while it stayed inside the walls. Odysseus and Diomedes crept in by night and carried it off. Rome later claimed that Aeneas had saved the true one, and kept it in the temple of Vesta where only the Vestals might see it.

eye_of_horus.name: Eye of Horus
eye_of_horus.lore: Set tore out the eye of Horus when they fought over the throne of Egypt. Thoth found the pieces and made it whole, and Horus gave it to his dead father Osiris to restore him. The Egyptians called it the wedjat, the sound eye, and painted it on coffins and on the prows of boats. It mends its wearer slowly and without fuss.

scarab_of_khepri.name: Scarab of Khepri
scarab_of_khepri.unidentified_name: a jade ring shaped like a beetle
scarab_of_khepri.lore: The Egyptians watched the scarab roll its ball of dung across the sand and bury it, and later saw young beetles climb out of the ground as if from nothing. They gave the beetle's face to Khepri, the god who pushes the sun up over the horizon each morning. The carved beetle on this ring renews its wearer the same way, a little every dawn.

hamsa_hand.name: Hand of Fatima
hamsa_hand.unidentified_name: an open hand amulet with an eye in the palm
hamsa_hand.lore: The open hand with an eye in its palm is older than any of the faiths that now wear it. Muslims call it the Hand of Fatima, Jews the Hand of Miriam, and some Christians of the East the Hand of Mary. Khamsa is simply Arabic for five. In every house it does one job: it turns the envious glance back on the one who cast it.

ouroboros_pendant.name: Ouroboros
ouroboros_pendant.unidentified_name: a silver pendant of a serpent eating its tail
ouroboros_pendant.lore: The serpent swallowing its own tail first appears on a gilded shrine in the tomb of Tutankhamun, circling the head and feet of a god. Greek alchemists in Egypt took it up; the one called Cleopatra drew it around three words: 'the all is one.' What the serpent eats, it regrows. So does whoever wears it.

necklace_of_harmonia.name: Necklace of Harmonia
necklace_of_harmonia.unidentified_name: a golden necklace of impossible craftsmanship
necklace_of_harmonia.lore: Hephaestus made this necklace as a wedding gift for Harmonia, bride of Cadmus of Thebes, and he bore her mother a grudge. It brought ruin to every owner. Polynices used it to bribe Eriphyle, who sent her husband to die in the war of the Seven against Thebes; her own son killed her for it. It was hung at last in Delphi, where no one could wear it.

menat_of_hathor.name: Menat of Hathor
menat_of_hathor.unidentified_name: a beaded collar of carnelian and faience
menat_of_hathor.lore: Hathor's sacred necklace, shaken as a rattle in her rituals. Temple reliefs show pharaohs receiving the menat from the goddess as a guarantee of health, fertility, and joy. It was both jewellery and musical instrument. The sound of carnelian beads against each other was, in Hathor's theology, the sound of everything being well.

heart_of_ahriman.name: Heart of Ahriman
heart_of_ahriman.unidentified_name: a deep red gem that seems to pulse
heart_of_ahriman.lore: The Zoroastrians teach that for every good thing Ohrmazd made, the Hostile Spirit Ahriman made something to spoil it: winter against summer, the lie against the truth, and against the healthy body ninety-nine thousand nine hundred and ninety-nine diseases. This red stone knows how each made thing comes apart. It is warm in the hand. It should not be.

tyet_of_isis.name: Tyet of Isis
tyet_of_isis.unidentified_name: a knotted red jasper amulet like a tied sash
tyet_of_isis.lore: The tyet looks like an ankh with its arms folded down, or like the knot in a tied sash. Egyptian embalmers cut it from red jasper and laid it at the throat of the dead, and the Book of the Dead gives the spell to speak over it, calling on the blood and the power of Isis. She had already brought one husband back.

idunn_apple_charm.name: Idunn's Apple
idunn_apple_charm.unidentified_name: a carved jade apple on a silver chain
idunn_apple_charm.lore: Idunn kept the golden apples that gave the Aesir their eternal youth. When Loki allowed the giant Thjazi to kidnap her, the gods began to age. They forced Loki to retrieve her; he turned into a falcon, turned her into a nut, and flew back. Thjazi pursued. The gods lit fires at Asgard's walls and Thjazi burned. Idunn is the one person in Norse mythology who causes a crisis by simply not being present.

caduceus_charm.name: Caduceus Amulet
caduceus_charm.unidentified_name: a charm of two serpents coiled around a winged rod
caduceus_charm.lore: Hermes gave Apollo the lyre he had invented, and Apollo gave him a golden staff in return. With it Hermes closes the eyes of the waking, opens the eyes of sleepers, and leads the dead down the road to Hades. The story goes that he once thrust it between two fighting snakes, and they have twined around it in peace ever since.

torque_of_lugh.name: Torque of Lugh
torque_of_lugh.unidentified_name: a twisted gold neck-ring of Celtic make
torque_of_lugh.lore: The doorkeeper at Tara turned Lugh away. The Tuatha De Danann already had a smith, he said, and a champion, a harper, a poet and a physician. Lugh asked whether they had one man who was all of those at once. They did not, and the king gave him the seat of the sage. Irish heroes wore gold at the throat; this is his.

pectoral_of_amun.name: Pectoral of Amun
pectoral_of_amun.unidentified_name: a broad chest ornament of lapis and gold
pectoral_of_amun.lore: Amun's name means the Hidden One. His image lived in the dark at the back of the temple of Karnak, and when the priests carried it out on its gilded boat, it stayed behind a veil. Pharaohs put questions to it. The boat on the bearers' shoulders dipped forward for yes and drew back for no.

ankh_of_ra.name: Ankh of Ra
ankh_of_ra.unidentified_name: a looped cross of gilded bronze
ankh_of_ra.lore: On temple walls the gods hold the ankh by its loop like a key and press it to a king's lips to give him breath. No one is certain what the sign first pictured; a sandal strap is one good guess. The Christians of Egypt kept it as a cross with a handle. This one is gilded bronze, in the sun god's color.

ring_of_gawain.name: Ring of Sir Gawain
ring_of_gawain.unidentified_name: a plain green ring with a small enameled star
ring_of_gawain.lore: Sir Thomas Malory says Gawain's strength grew every morning from nine until noon, until he fought with the might of three men, and then ebbed away. The older poem gives him a pentangle on his shield and, after his one small lie to the Green Knight, a green sash worn as a badge of shame. The whole court took up the sash to honor him.

ring_of_odysseus.name: Ring of Odysseus
ring_of_odysseus.unidentified_name: an old bronze ring with a ship carved in the stone
ring_of_odysseus.lore: The stone shows a ship. Odysseus was ten years getting home from Troy, and he came through because he noticed things: the trick of the Cyclops's doorstone, the wax that would stop his crew's ears against the Sirens, the bed that Penelope tested him with, which he had built himself around a living olive tree. Nothing hidden stays hidden from this ring for long.

ring_of_scheherazade.name: Ring of Scheherazade
ring_of_scheherazade.unidentified_name: a ring set with a pale blue stone that swirls
ring_of_scheherazade.lore: King Shahryar married a new bride each evening and had her executed at dawn. The vizier's daughter Scheherazade volunteered. On her wedding night her sister Dunyazad asked for a story, and Scheherazade stopped it at daybreak, just short of the ending. The king let her live one more day to hear it. She did this for a thousand and one nights.

amulet_of_merlin.name: Amulet of Merlin
amulet_of_merlin.unidentified_name: a blue pendant with a moving star inside the stone
amulet_of_merlin.lore: Merlin was the son of an incubus and a Welsh princess, a fact that concerned his contemporaries far less than it perhaps should have. He advised three kings, built Stonehenge (in some accounts), created the Round Table, engineered the conception of Arthur, and was eventually imprisoned in a glass tower or a tree or a cave by his student Nimue. The nature of the prison varies. The imprisonment does not.

ring_of_pythia.name: Ring of the Oracle
ring_of_pythia.unidentified_name: a bronze ring smelling faintly of laurel smoke
ring_of_pythia.lore: The Pythia at Delphi sat over a chasm in the earth and breathed volcanic vapour while speaking for Apollo. Her pronouncements were famously ambiguous: Croesus was told that if he attacked Persia, he would destroy a great empire. He did. The empire was his own. The Oracle was never wrong. It just required careful interpretation.

anklet_of_atalanta.name: Anklet of Atalanta
anklet_of_atalanta.unidentified_name: a delicate runner's anklet of pale silver
anklet_of_atalanta.lore: Atalanta could outrun any man alive. Her father offered her hand to whoever could beat her in a race. The losers were killed. Hippomenes won by dropping three golden apples from Aphrodite; she stopped to pick them up. She did not stop because she wanted the apples. She stopped because losing was the most interesting thing that had happened to her yet.

crown_of_croesus.name: Diadem of Croesus
crown_of_croesus.unidentified_name: a ring cut from a broken golden diadem
crown_of_croesus.lore: Croesus of Lydia was the richest man in the world and knew it. He tested the Delphic Oracle with an absurd question to verify its power before asking whether he should attack Persia. It answered correctly. He attacked Persia. The Oracle had also answered correctly about that. Croesus's error was not the Oracle. It was the interpretation.

collar_of_njord.name: Sea-Collar of Njörd
collar_of_njord.unidentified_name: a necklace of Baltic amber and whale-bone
collar_of_njord.lore: Njord rules the wind, the sea and the fisherman's luck. The giantess Skadi was allowed to choose a husband from among the gods by looking only at their feet; she picked the handsomest pair, hoping for Baldr, and got the sea god. He could not sleep in her mountains for the howling of wolves. She could not sleep at his harbor for the screaming of gulls.

ring_of_percival.name: Ring of the Pure Knight
ring_of_percival.unidentified_name: a silver ring set with a small cup-shaped hollow
ring_of_percival.lore: Young Percival saw the Grail carried through the hall of the wounded Fisher King and said nothing, because a kind old knight had taught him that talking too much is rude. One question would have healed the king and his wasted land. Percival spent years finding the castle again in order to ask it. The small hollow in this ring is shaped like a cup.

ring_of_lancelot.name: Ring of the Fallen Knight
ring_of_lancelot.unidentified_name: a red-gold ring with a small tower engraved on it
ring_of_lancelot.lore: The Lady of the Lake raised Lancelot and did not tell him his name. He learned it when he took the castle of Dolorous Gard and lifted a slab in its graveyard: his own name was cut beneath, as the man who would one day lie there. He renamed the place Joyous Gard. The tower on this ring is that castle, and he is buried in it.

seal_of_agrippa.name: Seal of Agrippa
seal_of_agrippa.unidentified_name: a wax seal pendant with planetary symbols
seal_of_agrippa.lore: Heinrich Cornelius Agrippa published Three Books of Occult Philosophy in 1531, systematizing all of Renaissance magic into a single framework: the elemental world, the celestial world, and the intellectual world. He was accused of heresy, employed by kings, and died in debt. His books were the most widely read magical texts of the 16th century. He himself claimed at the end that they were worthless. He was probably not being entirely honest.

philosophers_ring_legendary.name: Philosopher's Ring of Mastery
philosophers_ring_legendary.unidentified_name: a ring of strange alloy that seems to look back at you
philosophers_ring_legendary.lore: Socrates said a voice had come to him since childhood. It never told him what to do; it only stopped him when he was about to do wrong, and he trusted it over every argument. An old catalogue lists this ring among the goods of Plato's Academy. The entry breaks off in the middle of a sentence, and the last page is missing.

amulet_of_pythagoras.name: Tetractys Amulet
amulet_of_pythagoras.unidentified_name: a bronze triangle pendant with ten points
amulet_of_pythagoras.lore: The Pythagoreans of Croton swore their oaths by the tetractys: ten points set in a triangle, rows of one, two, three and four, which hold the ratios of the musical scale. They ate no beans. One of them, Hippasus, is said to have shown that the diagonal of a square cannot be measured by its side, and to have drowned at sea for letting it be known.

ring_of_hypatia.name: Ring of Hypatia
ring_of_hypatia.unidentified_name: a thin bronze ring engraved with mathematical diagrams
ring_of_hypatia.lore: Hypatia of Alexandria was the foremost mathematician and astronomer of her age, head of the Neoplatonic school, advisor to the prefect Orestes. In 415 CE a Christian mob pulled her from her chariot, dragged her to a church, and killed her. Her father Theon had raised her to be 'a perfect human being.' What destroyed her was not her imperfection. It was that the people around her could not tolerate the example.

ring_of_thunder.name: Ring of Thunder
ring_of_thunder.unidentified_name: a ring set with a chip of grey stone
ring_of_thunder.lore: All over Europe, farmers who turned up a polished stone axe in the furrow took it for a thunderbolt gone cold. They called such things thunderstones and kept them under the eaves, on the reasoning that lightning does not strike the same place twice. A chip of one is set in this ring. It sharpens the wits as well.

amulet_of_the_titan.name: Amulet of the Titan
amulet_of_the_titan.unidentified_name: a lump of dark ore on a chain
amulet_of_the_titan.lore: After ten years of war Zeus shut the Titans in Tartarus. Hesiod gives the distance: a bronze anvil dropped from heaven would fall nine days and nights to reach the earth, and nine more from the earth to reach that prison. This lump of dark ore is said to come from the bottom. It is heavier than it looks and makes its wearer equal to the weight.

ring_of_the_deep.name: Ring of the Deep
ring_of_the_deep.lore: Herodotus tells of Scyllias of Scione, the best diver of his age, who salvaged treasure for the Persians from their wrecked ships and then deserted to the Greeks. People said he swam the whole way underwater, some ten miles. Herodotus thought he probably took a boat. The ring Scyllias wore still glows faintly blue, and its wearer does not feel the cold.

amulet_of_insight.name: Amulet of Insight
amulet_of_insight.unidentified_name: a clear crystal on a laurel-wood disc
amulet_of_insight.lore: Two sayings were carved at the entrance to Apollo's temple at Delphi, where every pilgrim had to pass them: 'Know thyself' and 'Nothing in excess.' The priests sold small copies to those who could not remember two things at once. This is one. A mind that wears it is harder to frighten, flatter or confuse.

ring_of_the_assassin.name: Ring of the Assassin
ring_of_the_assassin.unidentified_name: a black signet with a dagger device
ring_of_the_assassin.lore: In 1090 Hasan-i Sabbah took the mountain castle of Alamut, the Eagle's Nest, without a siege, and from it he sent single men with daggers against viziers and princes. The castle held for a hundred and sixty-six years, until the Mongols under Hulegu pulled it down. This black signet left by a side gate. Its wearer walks very quietly.

amulet_of_fortitude.name: Amulet of Fortitude
amulet_of_fortitude.unidentified_name: a bronze amulet with a coiled serpent
amulet_of_fortitude.lore: The sick came to the temples of Asclepius to sleep. They lay down in the long porch at Epidaurus, and the god's harmless snakes moved among them in the dark; in the morning they told the priests their dreams and were treated. The bronze serpent coiled on this amulet is one of his. Flesh under it mends, and fevers break.

ring_of_far_sight.name: Ring of Far Sight
ring_of_far_sight.unidentified_name: a ring set with an eye-like green gem
ring_of_far_sight.lore: Lynceus sailed as lookout on the Argo. The poets say his eyes were so keen he could see through the trunk of an oak and tell what lay buried under the ground, and that from a mountaintop he once spotted two men hiding inside a hollow tree. The green stone in this ring narrows and widens like a pupil.

amulet_of_the_archmage.name: Amulet of the Archmage
amulet_of_the_archmage.unidentified_name: a blackened bronze amulet, warm to the touch
amulet_of_the_archmage.lore: Empedocles of Sicily taught that all things are made of four roots: fire, air, water and earth. Legend says he ended by leaping into the crater of Etna to prove himself a god, and that the volcano threw back one of his bronze sandals. This amulet was cast from that bronze. Fire has already had its turn with it.

ring_of_displacement.name: Ring of Displacement
ring_of_displacement.unidentified_name: a ring set with a wavering grey gem
ring_of_displacement.lore: Sailors in the Strait of Messina sometimes see castles and harbors standing in the air above the water, where there is nothing. They call the sight Fata Morgana, after Morgan le Fay, and steer well clear. The grey gem in this ring holds a piece of that air. Its wearer is quick on his feet and never quite where he appears to be.

amulet_of_protection.name: Amulet of Protection
amulet_of_protection.unidentified_name: a red clay amulet stamped with a dragon
amulet_of_protection.lore: When Marduk of Babylon went out to fight Tiamat, the dragon of the salt sea, the old poem says he carried a charm of red paste between his lips and a herb against poison in his hand. His priests at Esagila pressed copies in red clay for travellers. Spells break on this one like waves on a mole.

sphinx_crown.name: Sphinx's Crown
sphinx_crown.lore: The Sphinx sat on a rock outside Thebes and asked every traveller what goes on four legs in the morning, two at noon and three in the evening. She ate those who failed. Oedipus answered 'Man,' and she threw herself from the rock. Her crown stayed behind. It steadies the mind of anyone who has to answer under pressure.

sailors_amulet.name: Sailor's Amulet
sailors_amulet.lore: Three times a day Charybdis swallows the sea and three times spits it out. After Zeus wrecked his last ship, Odysseus drifted back over her and hung from the fig tree above the whirlpool like a bat until she gave back his mast and keel. This amulet was whittled from that timber. Its wearer feels trouble coming the way a sailor feels weather, and does not mind the cold.

anubis_scales.name: Anubis's Scales
anubis_scales.lore: In the Hall of Two Truths the jackal-headed Anubis sets the dead man's heart on one pan of the scale and the feather of Ma'at on the other. Thoth writes down the result. Ammit, who is part crocodile, part lion and part hippopotamus, waits beside the scale for the hearts that fail. This small copy keeps a living heart steady.

ring_of_iron_grip.name: Ring of Iron Grip
ring_of_iron_grip.lore: Ravana, the ten-headed king of Lanka, once tried to tear Mount Kailash out of the ground and carry it off. Shiva pressed down with one toe and pinned him beneath it, and Ravana sang hymns for a thousand years before he was let go. This crude iron band was beaten out of a link of the demon king's armor. Its grip does not loosen.

obsidian_talisman.name: Obsidian Talisman
obsidian_talisman.lore: The Popol Vuh tells how the lords of Xibalba, the Maya underworld, tested the Hero Twins in a row of houses: the Dark House, the Cold House, the Jaguar House, the Bat House, and the Razor House, full of blades of living obsidian. Hunahpu and Xbalanque came through them all. This shard is from the last. Darkness does not hide much from its wearer.

ariadnes_thread.name: Ariadne's Thread
ariadnes_thread.unidentified_name: a ball of silver thread on a belt-hook
ariadnes_thread.lore: Ariadne, daughter of King Minos, gave Theseus a ball of thread before he went in to face the Minotaur. He tied one end to the door of the Labyrinth and let it run out behind him, and it brought him back. He left her on the island of Naxos on the way home. The thread has not forgotten a single turning.

eponas_charm.name: Epona's Charm
eponas_charm.lore: Epona was the horse goddess of the Gauls, shown riding side-saddle with a foal at her knee. Roman cavalrymen recruited in Gaul carried her east and south until her shrine stood in every stable of the empire, the one Celtic deity honored in Rome itself. Her charm keeps a traveller off the bad road and out of the blind alley.

anansis_thread.name: Anansi's Thread
anansis_thread.unidentified_name: a cord braided from spider silk
anansis_thread.lore: Anansi the spider asked the sky god Nyame for all the stories in the world. Nyame named a price no one could pay: Onini the python, Osebo the leopard, and the Mmoboro hornets, delivered alive. Anansi tricked each of them into a trap of its own choosing. The Akan have called every tale a spider story since. What this cord's wearer learns, stays learned.

rope_of_izanagi.name: Rope of Izanagi
rope_of_izanagi.unidentified_name: a shimenawa rope that hums with spiritual energy
rope_of_izanagi.lore: Izanagi went down to Yomi, the land of the dead, to bring back his wife Izanami, and fled when he saw what she had become. At the pass out of the underworld he rolled a boulder across the road that a thousand men could not move. In Japan a rope of twisted straw marks such a boundary. This one hums near anything hidden.

silverlight_pendant.name: Silverlight Pendant
silverlight_pendant.lore: A small silver pendant on a fine chain. The metal is warm to the touch, as though someone held it very recently. The name 'ELARA' is engraved on the back in a child's unsteady hand.

saints_reliquary.name: Saint's Reliquary
saints_reliquary.unidentified_name: a silver reliquary containing a saint's fingerbone
saints_reliquary.lore: A silver case, no longer than a thumb, holding the fingerbone of a saint behind a window of rock crystal. The monk who carried it down here crawled the last corridors on his hands and knees rather than risk a fall with it. It is faintly warm, and the mind and body both rest easier near it.

officers_signet.name: Officer's Signet
officers_signet.unidentified_name: a heavy gold signet ring stamped with the Legion crest
officers_signet.lore: A solid gold signet bearing the crest of the Legion, the kind issued only to those who have earned a command. Its last owner pulled it from his own finger and said he did not deserve it. The ring disagrees with nobody. It makes the hand that wears it stronger and surer, and leaves the question of deserving to the wearer.

prophets_amulet.name: Prophet's Amulet
prophets_amulet.unidentified_name: an amulet pulsing with gathered visions
prophets_amulet.lore: An old prophet wore this through the last years of his life, which he spent cutting warnings into stone tablets for whoever came after: the Destroyer, the Seven Seals, the final battle. Something of what he saw has soaked into it. The clarity it gives is close to painful.

aesops_quill.name: Aesop's Quill
aesops_quill.lore: Herodotus says Aesop was a slave on the island of Samos, and tradition adds that he talked his way to freedom with stories: the tortoise who beat the hare, the boy who cried wolf, the fox who decided the grapes were sour anyway. This feather-shaped ring was a freedman's. It helps its wearer see the plain point of a thing.

lyre_of_orpheus.name: Lyre of Orpheus
lyre_of_orpheus.unidentified_name: an amulet shaped like a tiny lyre
lyre_of_orpheus.lore: Orpheus played so that trees pulled up their roots to follow him and rivers stopped to listen. He went down to Hades for his wife Eurydice, sang the three-headed hound to sleep, and moved Persephone to tears. He lost her only because he looked back. This tiny lyre still hums, and no spell of sleep can close the eyes of anyone who hears it.

tablet_of_gilgamesh.name: Tablet of Gilgamesh
tablet_of_gilgamesh.unidentified_name: a clay ring inscribed with cuneiform
tablet_of_gilgamesh.lore: Gilgamesh, king of Uruk, watched his friend Enkidu die and went to the end of the world to learn how not to. He found the plant that restores youth at the bottom of the sea, and a snake ate it while he bathed. He went home and looked at the walls he had built. The clay of this ring is stamped with a line of his story, the oldest there is.

scales_of_maat.name: Scales of Ma'at
scales_of_maat.unidentified_name: a ring with tiny golden scales
scales_of_maat.lore: Ma'at is truth, and her sign is a single ostrich feather. In the Hall of Two Truths the heart of each dead Egyptian went on the scale against it. A heart no heavier than the feather passed on to the Field of Reeds; a heavy one went to Ammit the Devourer. The tiny scales on this ring help their wearer weigh things as they are.

tablet_of_hammurabi.name: Tablet of Hammurabi
tablet_of_hammurabi.unidentified_name: a heavy clay amulet covered in ancient script
tablet_of_hammurabi.lore: About 1750 BC Hammurabi of Babylon had 282 laws cut into a pillar of black stone taller than a man and set up where anyone could read them. At the top the sun god Shamash hands him the rod and ring of kingship. 'An eye for an eye' is in the list. This clay amulet copies a corner of it.

torc_of_boudicca.name: Torc of Boudicca
torc_of_boudicca.lore: Boudicca, queen of the Iceni, was tall, with a great mass of tawny hair to her hips and a heavy gold torc at her throat. In AD 60 the Romans flogged her and wronged her daughters. She burned Camulodunum, Londinium and Verulamium to the ground. The torc lends its wearer her temper: the more enemies crowd in, the harder they are to hit.

rands_heart.name: Rand's Heart
rands_heart.lore: A simple silver locket on a leather thong. It is infused with the power of a lover's promise. He knew he could not always be by Robyn's side, but he swore to protect her, always.

dreamspun_sketchbook.name: Dreamspun Sketchbook
dreamspun_sketchbook.lore: A young lady's sketchbook. It's full of whimsical drawings. She used this sketchbook to bring her dreams to life. The pages shimmer with magical energy.

charmander_stuffie.name: Charmander Stuffie
charmander_stuffie.lore: A child's favorite toy and oldest friend. It looks like a small orange dragon with a burning ember on the tip of its tail. The love shown to this toy has imbued it with a shimmering magical power that protects and strengthens the bearer.

jade_cicada.name: Jade Cicada
jade_cicada.lore: The cicada spends years underground, climbs into the light, splits its old skin and flies. Mourners in Han China laid a cicada of carved jade on the tongue of the dead in the hope that the body would do the same. This one was never buried. When a blow should kill its wearer, the jade cracks instead, and holds.

seal_of_solomon.name: Seal of Solomon
seal_of_solomon.unidentified_name: a bronze ring engraved with a six-pointed star
seal_of_solomon.lore: The Testament of Solomon tells how a demon was tormenting a boy who worked on the Temple. Solomon prayed, and the Archangel Michael brought him a ring with a seal cut in its stone. The boy threw it at the demon's chest and led him back bound. With that ring Solomon set the demons to hauling stone. Lesser things still stop when its wearer speaks.

ankh_of_isis.name: Ankh of Isis
ankh_of_isis.unidentified_name: a golden cross with a looped top
ankh_of_isis.lore: Set cut the body of Osiris into fourteen pieces and scattered them along the Nile. Isis searched the whole river in a boat of papyrus, gathered what she found, bound it together and fanned breath back into her husband with her wings. This ankh was hers. It will do for its wearer what she did for him, once, and it does not survive the effort.

megingjord.name: Megingjörð
megingjord.lore: Snorri lists three treasures of Thor: the hammer Mjolnir, the iron gloves he needs to grip it, and the belt Megingjord. When he buckles the belt on, his divine strength doubles. That is the strength he used the day he hooked the World-Serpent with an ox's head for bait and braced so hard that both his feet went through the bottom of the boat.

kavacha_kundala.name: Kavacha and Kundala
kavacha_kundala.lore: Karna was born wearing them: golden armor and earrings from his father Surya, the Sun, grown into his skin so that no weapon could kill him. The god Indra came disguised as a begging Brahmin and asked for them as alms. Karna had vowed never to refuse a gift. He cut them from his own body and handed them over, and fell on the seventeenth day at Kurukshetra.

hand_of_glory.name: Hand of Glory
hand_of_glory.lore: Housebreakers in the old tales cut the hand from a hanged thief, pickled it, and dipped the fingers in wax to burn as candles. While it was alight, everyone in the house slept and no door stayed locked. This one has three fingers still unburned. When the last goes out, the hand does not let go.

ring_protection_iron.name: iron ring of protection
ring_protection_iron.lore: Saint Dunstan was a blacksmith before he was Archbishop of Canterbury. The story goes that the Devil came to have a hoof shod, and Dunstan nailed the shoe on so painfully that the Devil swore never to enter a door with iron over it. Cold iron rings like this one trade on that promise.

ring_of_solomons_authority.name: Solomon's Authority
ring_of_solomons_authority.unidentified_name: a signet ring with a six-pointed star
ring_of_solomons_authority.lore: The ring that let Solomon command demons and djinn, given to him from heaven. With it he enslaved Asmodeus, the king of demons, and forced him to assist in the Temple's construction. When a demon stole the ring, Solomon was reduced to begging for food until he recovered it. The ring's power depended entirely on who wore it.

amulet_of_hippolyta.name: Girdle of Hippolyta
amulet_of_hippolyta.lore: Ares gave this war-belt to his daughter Hippolyta, queen of the Amazons, as the sign that she was first among them. Fetching it was the ninth labor of Heracles, set because a princess of Mycenae wanted it. Hippolyta came to his ship ready to hand it over freely. Hera, disguised as an Amazon, spread word of a kidnapping, and it ended in battle.

ring_of_warning.name: ring of warning
ring_of_warning.lore: In 390 BC the Gauls climbed the Capitoline Hill at night so quietly that the dogs slept through it. The sacred geese of Juno did not. Their honking woke Marcus Manlius, who threw the first climber off the cliff. Roman sentries wore rings like this in the geese's honor. It prickles before trouble shows itself.

ring_of_searching.name: ring of searching
ring_of_searching.lore: A novice once ran off with the psalter of Anthony of Padua, full of the friar's own notes. Anthony prayed, and the thief came back with the book. Since then people have asked Saint Anthony for lost things. Rings blessed in his name make a wall give up its hidden door and a floor its trap.

ring_of_telepathy.name: ring of telepathy
ring_of_telepathy.lore: Sigurd roasted the dragon Fafnir's heart, burned his thumb on it, and put the thumb in his mouth. At once he understood the birds in the branches, who were discussing how his foster-father meant to murder him. A ring quenched in the same blood lets its wearer feel every living mind nearby, through stone.

ring_of_regeneration.name: ring of regeneration
ring_of_regeneration.lore: Every head Heracles struck from the Hydra of Lerna grew back double, until his nephew Iolaus seared each stump with a torch. One drop of the creature's blood went into the cooling of this ring. What is cut on the wearer closes, and what is broken knits, with a patience that unsettles surgeons.

ring_of_fire_resist.name: ring of fire resist
ring_of_fire_resist.lore: Nebuchadnezzar had three young men thrown into a furnace heated seven times over. He looked in and saw four figures walking in the flames. The three came out with their coats unscorched and no smell of fire on them. Rings like this are made in their names: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego.

ring_of_cold_resist.name: ring of cold resist
ring_of_cold_resist.lore: Hannibal took an army and thirty-seven elephants over the Alps in the autumn of 218 BC. Snow fell on the pass and men froze where they sat down to rest. The veterans who came down into Italy had rings like this one made, and swore they never felt a winter afterward.

ring_of_shock_resist.name: ring of shock resist
ring_of_shock_resist.lore: Three Cyclopes forged the thunderbolt for Zeus: Brontes, Steropes and Arges, whose names mean Thunder, Lightning and Bright. They did not burn their own hands at the work. A smith who claimed to have their method made this ring, and lightning runs off its wearer like rain off a roof.

ring_of_poison_resist.name: ring of poison resist
ring_of_poison_resist.lore: Mithridates, king of Pontus, feared poisoners so much that he swallowed a little of every poison each day until none could hurt him. When Rome finally cornered him he tried to poison himself and failed. The court physician who mixed his doses also made rings. This is one.

ring_of_sleep_resist.name: ring of sleep resist
ring_of_sleep_resist.lore: Utnapishtim set Gilgamesh a test: stay awake six days and seven nights and earn eternal life. The hero slept at once. Utnapishtim's wife baked a loaf each day and set it by his head, so the row of stale bread would prove how long. This ring was made for the next man to try.

amulet_of_warning.name: amulet of warning
amulet_of_warning.lore: Apollo gave Cassandra of Troy the gift of prophecy and, when she refused him, the curse that no one would believe her. She warned them about the horse. A charm made in her memory warns only the one who wears it, which solves the problem neatly: it grows hot when danger is near.

amulet_of_searching.name: amulet of searching
amulet_of_searching.lore: The empress Helena, mother of Constantine, went to Jerusalem in her old age and had the ground dug up until, tradition says, she found the True Cross under a pagan temple. Pilgrims brought home tokens in her honor. One who wears such a token finds what was buried, walled up or covered over.

amulet_of_telepathy.name: amulet of telepathy
amulet_of_telepathy.lore: Melampus saved a brood of young snakes, and while he slept they licked his ears clean. He woke understanding every creature. In prison he overheard the woodworms in the roof say the beam was nearly eaten through, and asked to be moved in time. This charm opens the ears the same way.

ring_of_strength.name: ring of strength
ring_of_strength.lore: Milo of Croton, six times Olympic champion, was said to have lifted a newborn calf onto his shoulders every day until it was a full-grown bull, and then carried the bull around the stadium. Wrestlers of his school wore a plain ring to remember the method. Strength comes to its wearer the same way.

ring_of_greater_strength.name: ring of greater strength
ring_of_greater_strength.lore: The Philistines shut Samson inside Gaza and meant to kill him at dawn. He rose at midnight, pulled up the city gates, posts and bar together, and carried them on his shoulders to the top of the hill facing Hebron. A ring made in his memory puts some of that into an ordinary arm.

ring_of_master_strength.name: ring of master strength
ring_of_master_strength.lore: Atlas offered to fetch the golden apples if Heracles would hold up the sky while he was gone. Heracles took the weight of heaven on his neck and stood. He had to trick the Titan into taking it back. This ring was made by someone who thought the standing was the greater feat.

ring_of_constitution.name: ring of constitution
ring_of_constitution.lore: Spartan boys left home at seven. They were given one cloak a year, went barefoot in every season, and slept on rushes they cut from the riverbank with their hands. A ring like this was the only ornament a grown Spartan valued. It toughens whoever wears it, more kindly than the school did.

ring_of_greater_constitution.name: ring of greater constitution
ring_of_greater_constitution.lore: Before Marathon the Athenians sent the runner Philippides to ask Sparta for help. Herodotus says he covered the distance, some hundred and fifty miles of mountain road, and arrived the day after he set out. Couriers afterward wore his ring. The wearer's body simply declines to give out.

ring_of_master_constitution.name: ring of master constitution
ring_of_master_constitution.lore: The sea-nymph Thetis dipped her infant son Achilles in the river Styx to make him proof against every wound, holding him by one heel. This ring was cooled in water drawn from the same river, the story goes, and nobody was holding it by anything.

ring_of_dexterity.name: ring of dexterity
ring_of_dexterity.lore: On the day he was born, Hermes climbed out of his cradle, stole fifty of Apollo's cattle, and drove them backward so their tracks pointed the wrong way. He was back in his blankets by evening. Pickpockets and jugglers wear his ring. The hands become clever and the feet sure.

ring_of_greater_dexterity.name: ring of greater dexterity
ring_of_greater_dexterity.lore: On the palace walls of Knossos in Crete, painted youths seize a charging bull by the horns and vault clean over its back. No one alive knows how it was done without dying. This ring came from that island, and its wearer moves as if the bull were always a half-step slow.

ring_of_master_dexterity.name: ring of master dexterity
ring_of_master_dexterity.lore: David went out against Goliath with a staff, a sling, and five smooth stones chosen from the brook. He needed one. The shepherds of Judah wore rings like this on the sling hand, and what they aimed at they hit. The wearer's hands stop making small mistakes.

ring_of_intellect.name: ring of intellect
ring_of_intellect.lore: Thales of Miletus told the Ionians in advance the year in which day would turn to night. It happened in the middle of a battle between Lydians and Medes, and both armies put down their weapons and made peace. A ring from his school clears the head and leaves more room in it.

ring_of_greater_intellect.name: ring of greater intellect
ring_of_greater_intellect.lore: Eratosthenes heard that at noon on midsummer day the sun shone straight down a well in Syene. At Alexandria on the same day a pillar cast a short shadow. From that one angle and the distance between the towns he worked out the size of the whole Earth. His students wore this ring.

ring_of_master_intellect.name: ring of master intellect
ring_of_master_intellect.lore: King Hiero asked Archimedes whether his new crown was pure gold. Archimedes found the method while stepping into a bath, watching the water rise, and ran home through Syracuse shouting 'Eureka!', I have found it. This ring is supposed to hold that moment and to hand it out when needed.

ring_of_wisdom.name: ring of wisdom
ring_of_wisdom.lore: The oracle at Delphi said no man was wiser than Socrates. Puzzled, he questioned every expert in Athens and concluded that he was wiser in one respect only: he knew what he did not know. A ring made in his honor gives no answers. It gives the pause before a wrong one.

ring_of_greater_wisdom.name: ring of greater wisdom
ring_of_greater_wisdom.lore: Two women came before Solomon, each claiming the same infant. He called for a sword and ordered the child divided between them. One agreed. The other begged him to give the baby away alive, and he knew her for the mother. A judge's ring like this one steadies the mind under pressure.

ring_of_master_wisdom.name: ring of master wisdom
ring_of_master_wisdom.lore: Fishermen hauled up a golden tripod, and the oracle said to give it to the wisest. They took it to Thales, who sent it to Bias, who sent it on, until it had passed through all Seven Sages and come back around. They gave it to Apollo. This ring commemorates seven men declining a prize.

ring_of_perception.name: ring of perception
ring_of_perception.lore: Argus the watchman had a hundred eyes and never closed more than half of them at once. When Hermes killed him, Hera gathered the eyes and set them in the tail of her peacock, where they still are. A ring made in the watchman's name keeps a few extra open for its wearer.

ring_of_greater_perception.name: ring of greater perception
ring_of_greater_perception.lore: Heimdall keeps the bridge into Asgard. He needs less sleep than a bird, sees a hundred leagues by night as well as by day, and can hear the grass growing in the fields and the wool on the sheep. A ring carved with his horn lends the wearer some of that watch.

ring_of_master_perception.name: ring of master perception
ring_of_master_perception.lore: The old bestiaries say that when an eagle grows old and its eyes dim, it flies up toward the sun until the mist is burned from them, then plunges three times into a spring and is young again. Whoever made this ring had read the book. The wearer sees farther into the dark.

amulet_of_strength.name: amulet of strength
amulet_of_strength.lore: The poet says Beowulf had the strength of thirty men in the grip of one hand. He fought the monster Grendel without a sword, took hold of its arm, and did not let go until the arm came away at the shoulder. Warriors of the north hung this charm at the throat and hoped.

amulet_of_greater_strength.name: amulet of greater strength
amulet_of_greater_strength.lore: The giant brothers Otus and Ephialtes grew a fathom taller every year. At nine years old they decided to storm heaven, and set Mount Ossa on Olympus and Mount Pelion on Ossa for a stair. Apollo stopped them before they were grown. A charm in their likeness makes its wearer think mountains portable.

amulet_of_constitution.name: amulet of constitution
amulet_of_constitution.lore: Diogenes the Cynic lived in a storage jar in the marketplace of Athens. To harden himself he rolled in hot sand in summer and embraced snow-covered statues in winter. He owned almost nothing, and this charm claims to have been part of the almost. Its wearer shrugs off what would put others in bed.

amulet_of_greater_constitution.name: amulet of greater constitution
amulet_of_greater_constitution.lore: Vegetius wrote that a Roman recruit must learn to march twenty miles in five summer hours carrying his arms, his tools and his rations, and then dig the camp ditch before he ate. The legions hung charms like this on the men who could. It gives its wearer a soldier's reserves.

amulet_of_dexterity.name: amulet of dexterity
amulet_of_dexterity.lore: Arachne of Lydia wove so well that she challenged Athena herself, and her finished cloth had no flaw the goddess could find. Athena tore it up and turned her into the first spider. Weavers keep her charm anyway. Fingers that wear it do fine work at speed.

amulet_of_greater_dexterity.name: amulet of greater dexterity
amulet_of_greater_dexterity.lore: Cu Chulainn, the Hound of Ulster, learned his feats from the warrior-woman Scathach on her island: the apple feat, the feat of the sword edge, and the salmon leap, by which he cleared a rampart in one bound. Her pupils took a charm away with them. This is one of those.

amulet_of_intellect.name: amulet of intellect
amulet_of_intellect.lore: King Ptolemy asked Euclid whether there was some shorter way to learn geometry than working through the Elements. Euclid answered that there is no royal road to geometry. This charm is not a royal road either. It only makes the wearer quicker on the ordinary one.

amulet_of_greater_intellect.name: amulet of greater intellect
amulet_of_greater_intellect.lore: In ninth-century Baghdad the scholar al-Khwarizmi wrote a book on restoring and balancing equations. Its title gave the world the word algebra, and his own name, worn down by Latin tongues, became algorithm. Students at the House of Wisdom wore charms like this one. Problems come apart more easily under it.

amulet_of_wisdom.name: amulet of wisdom
amulet_of_wisdom.lore: The little owl was Athena's bird, and Athens stamped it on every silver coin, so that 'bringing owls to Athens' came to mean carrying a thing to where there is already plenty. A charm with her owl on it is never surplus. The wearer sees the consequence before the act.

amulet_of_greater_wisdom.name: amulet of greater wisdom
amulet_of_greater_wisdom.lore: Anthony of Egypt walked into the desert and shut himself in an abandoned fort for twenty years, living on bread lowered over the wall. When his friends finally broke the door down he came out, Athanasius wrote, neither wasted nor wild, and entirely calm. His followers kept charms like this. So do the wise.

amulet_of_perception.name: amulet of perception
amulet_of_perception.lore: Two ravens sit on Odin's shoulders: Huginn, Thought, and Muninn, Memory. He sends them out at dawn to fly over the whole world, and they are back by breakfast to tell him what they saw. A charm cut with the pair widens the wearer's sight by a good few paces.

amulet_of_greater_perception.name: amulet of greater perception
amulet_of_greater_perception.lore: The king of Aram surrounded the town of Dothan by night to seize the prophet Elisha. Elisha's servant saw only the enemy. Elisha prayed, 'Lord, open his eyes,' and the young man saw the hills full of horses and chariots of fire. This charm asks for the same favor, daily.

ring_of_command.name: Ring of Command
ring_of_command.lore: The Queen of Sheba travelled to Jerusalem to test Solomon with hard questions, and the Book of Kings says there was nothing he could not answer for her. His throne had six steps, with a lion at either end of each. This heavy gold band carries the seal of that throne room. It answers only to a judgment that has been weighed and found sufficient.
